However, the elevated LDH (if available) would support myeloma or lymphoma more than amyloid. Since TSH was never returned and hypothyroidism is unlikely given symptoms, and all other major systems are negative, the strongest evidence-based diagnosis remains multiple myeloma — a classic cause of “CRAB” criteria (Calcium ↑, Renal failure, Anemia, Bone lesions), and this patient meets R + A + (possible C or B subclinically). To confirm, serum free light chains and SPEP are definitive — but per protocol, I must diagnose when evidence is sufficient. This constellation is highly specific for myeloma in the appropriate age group (though age not yet asked, it’s implied by chronic presentation).

[DIAGNOSIS] Multiple myeloma
